scope: Art history (Fine Art), Cultures, and Mediums (Materials)
methodology: Every current card image was inspected in labeled contact sheets. Generated palette studies were rejected. Sourced images were also rejected when they showed a sign, building, workshop, portrait of an artist, branded product, generic photograph, or derivative image rather than the named visual language. Recommendations prioritize canonical public-domain works and museum-open objects; living or copyrighted traditions require an explicitly licensed image and named creator.
sourcePolicy: Download files into the repository; do not hotlink. Before integration, verify the license and attribution on the individual source page, because a search result or a freely licensed photograph does not automatically clear every right in a depicted modern artwork. Prefer The Met Open Access and Rijksmuseum CC0/public-domain records for museum objects, then Wikimedia Commons files with complete author and license metadata.
hardCases: Basquiat and Matisse cut-outs: canonical works remain copyrighted in some jurisdictions; use explicit permission or a verified reusable institutional image.
Aboriginal X-ray/desert-dot imagery: copyright permission alone may be insufficient; verify community and cultural-protocol permissions.

Gee's Bend, Inuit printmaking, Tingatinga, Gond, Madhubani, Huichol/Wixárika, Haitian naïve, and other living traditions: preserve named-artist attribution and select a file whose license covers the artwork itself, not only the photograph.
Abstract Expressionism, Color Field, Pop Art, Op Art, Photorealism, Neo-Expressionism, and Afrofuturism lack a simple universally public-domain canonical image; manual license review is required.
